description: I’m a CSE student interested in AI, web development, and space technology. I’m working on LunaLink, a browser-based NASA-data project that makes the Earth–Moon system interactive through 3D visualization, gestures, and voice. I’m looking for teammates interested in Three.js, NASA APIs/data, AI/ML, MediaPipe, UI/UX, web development, or creative problem-solving to help turn the idea into a working prototype.
summary:
LunaLink is a free, browser-based interactive tool that helps students understand the Earth–Moon system using real NASA data. Instead of relying on static 2D diagrams, LunaLink presents the Moon’s phases, orbit, distance, tides, and eclipses through an interactive 3D experience. Users can explore different dates and interact with the visualization using hand gestures and voice commands, making learning more engaging and accessible.

LunaLink uses NASA Scientific Visualization Studio data for Moon phase and libration information and NASA/JPL Horizons for lunar positions. The project is designed to run on a basic laptop with a webcam, without requiring installation, accounts, or paid services. By combining accurate space data with intuitive interaction and visual explanations, LunaLink aims to make difficult astronomy concepts easier to explore, understand, and remember.
details:
LunaLink is an interactive astronomy learning website developed by Team ApexTech to help students, teachers, and space enthusiasts explore the relationship between Earth and the Moon. It brings Moon phases, lunar orbits, eclipses, educational tide visualizations, a lunar calendar, and an Artemis mission replay together in one browser-based experience.

Users can select a date and explore calculated Moon information through interactive visualizations. Our “Ask Luna” assistant accepts typed questions or supported voice commands, explains astronomy concepts, and navigates the application. Its responses come from astronomy calculations and a curated knowledge base. Optional hand gestures let users move through dates, switch views, and control playback using a webcam. Quizzes and personalized birthday Moon cards make learning more engaging.

The main benefit is turning abstract astronomy concepts into experiences that learners can see, control, and question. Teachers can use LunaLink for classroom demonstrations, while students can explore independently through guest access. Our intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, strengthen understanding of lunar phenomena, and make space education more approachable through everyday technology.

We developed LunaLink using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with HTML Canvas for visualizations. The browser’s Web Speech API supports voice recognition and spoken responses, while Google MediaPipe supports hand-gesture recognition. NASA imagery supplements the calculated Moon views when available. Netlify hosts the website, Netlify Identity manages accounts and saved profile information, and Node.js with esbuild supports deployment preparation. Users need a compatible web browser; a microphone and webcam are optional for voice and gesture features. No specialized astronomy hardware is required.

LunaLink’s creativity comes from combining visual exploration, conversational guidance, gesture controls, and personalized learning activities in one astronomy experience. Learners can ask about a lunar event, explore the corresponding view, and test their understanding through a quiz.

Our team considered scientific clarity, ease of use, responsive design, privacy, browser compatibility, and internet availability. Camera and microphone features require permission, and typed input and conventional controls provide alternatives. Tide curves are labeled as educational illustrations, and the Artemis replay is distinguished from live mission telemetry. These choices help users understand both the learning value and the limits of the prototype.
